episode_title: 61. Scaling Culture Across Every Branch w/ Chris Turner

real_qa.q: How did Piedmont Services Group scale culture across its 11-12 locations?
real_qa.r: Piedmont identified the challenge that as they grew through acquisitions and geographic expansion, their culture became harder to maintain without a systematic approach. They hired Lee as Culture and Employee Development manager in 2022, then partnered with CultureWise in 2023 to create and deploy 31 fundamental behaviors across all branches. The 31 fundamentals, called the Piedmont Way, gave every location a common language and clear expectations that could be consistently reinforced through new hire onboarding and ongoing practices.
real_qa.requete: Piedmont Services Group culture 31 fundamentals scaling

real_qa.q: What impact has practicing 31 fundamentals had on Piedmont Services Group's consistency?
real_qa.r: The biggest impact Chris Turner cites is consistency—what he calls 'every branch speaking English but without their own dialect.' New hires now spend four hours of a day-and-a-half in onboarding learning the 31 fundamentals, so whether they work in Myrtle Beach or Richmond, they share the same expectations and accountability language. Employees hold each other accountable to behaviors like 'Be vigilant about safety' and 'Speak straight,' transforming culture from unspoken assumptions into actionable, enforceable practices across all locations.
real_qa.requete: Piedmont Services Group fundamentals consistency impact

real_qa.q: Why did Piedmont Services Group choose 31 fundamentals instead of 5 core values?
real_qa.r: Chris Turner and the leadership team did not start with a number in mind. During an offsite leadership meeting, they reviewed the CultureWise catalog of fundamentals and organically selected 31 because each one felt essential—they could not identify behaviors worth removing. Turner explains: 'I wouldn't change 31. I wouldn't make it 33 to 29. It's not too much. I think it's company specific.' He notes that the initial brainstorm produced about 40-45 potential behaviors, and trying to cut further would mean sacrificing things genuinely important to the company.

real_qa.q: How has the Piedmont Way language become embedded in Piedmont Services Group operations?
real_qa.r: The common language of the 31 fundamentals has become organic and reflexive—employees now say 'permission to speak straight for a minute' in daily conversations, embedding behaviors into the organization's vocabulary. More tellingly, branches have organically created their own 'Most Represents the Piedmont Way' award at company events, with technicians competing to embody the fundamentals. Turner notes: 'That was not something like, hey, each branch is going to do an award. No, it grew up from the branches.' This organic adoption signals full internalization of the culture.
real_qa.requete: Piedmont Way language embedded culture award

real_qa.q: How did hiring Lee from Chick-fil-A strengthen Piedmont Services Group's culture rollout?
real_qa.r: In 2022, Piedmont hired Lee, who came from Chick-fil-A with ministry background and strong communication skills, as Culture and Employee Development manager. Turner describes him as 'a ZZ Top, big biker beard looking guy, sleeve tattoos'—deliberately not a typical suit-wearing HR type. This authenticity was critical for credibility with the blue-collar technician workforce. Lee helped substantiate and disperse the culture across branches, then when Turner brought him to a Vistage presentation featuring CultureWise, Lee and Turner immediately committed to the framework, combining Lee's infrastructure and CultureWise's methodology.

guest.bio_context: Chris Turner joined Piedmont Services Group in 2003 as a construction sales engineer and rose through the company over two decades, holding various leadership roles including leading the building automation group. He was identified as successor to the retiring president in 2023 and became president at the beginning of 2024. He attended NC State as an engineer and initially worked at Corning before joining Piedmont post-9/11.
